transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because I... I snapped on a board call the other day. It was over a really small question about the facility budget, nothing that should have set me off, but I just lost my temper. And that is not how I run my company, and it's definitely not how I treat people. So, I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
Has this kind of outburst happened before, or was this the first time you've reacted this way in such a situation?

No, never. I mean, I can be firm, sure, you have to be in my position. But I don't lose control like that. It was completely out of character for me. That's why it bothered me enough to make an appointment. I just... I don't know where it came from.
Have you been under more stress than usual lately, or has anything significant been going on in your life recently?

Well, yeah, there has been. This whole thing... my reaction on the call, I mean... it's really been going on for about six days. I was doing a routine walkthrough at one of our facilities, and... well, there was an explosion. A fire broke out while we were in there. So, yeah, ever since that happened, I guess things have just been a lot more tense.
Since the explosion, have you noticed that you've been more irritable, angry, or having trouble managing your emotions in other situations as well?

Well, no, not really. I mean... I might be a little tense, sure, but I haven't been yelling at my staff or anything. That call was the only time I actually snapped. I've just been trying to keep things moving at work, so... no, I haven't really noticed it happening anywhere else.
Since the explosion, have you been feeling down, hopeless, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Well, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless. I'm a pragmatic guy, I know we'll rebuild the facility. But... I guess I have lost interest in things, yeah. Or not lost interest, exactly, but... things just feel flat. 

Usually, to unwind, I'll work on a chess problem, or go over my notes for my next hiking trip. Even just having a quiet dinner with my wife. Those things usually settle me right down. But lately, since the fire... I just can't seem to get any enjoyment out of them. It's like I know I should be enjoying it, but I just can't get there right now.
Since the explosion, have you noticed a drop in your energy levels or been feeling unusually fatigued?

No, I wouldn't say that. My energy levels have been pretty much normal. I mean, I'm still putting in my usual hours at work and keeping up with everything that needs to get done. So, no, I haven't felt unusually tired or dragged out.
Since the explosion, have you had any unwanted thoughts, memories, or flashbacks about the event that have been bothering you?

Yeah, I have. It happens a lot when I'm trying to work. I'll be right in the middle of a phone call, or just looking over some numbers, and... the blast just jumps back into my head. That fire by the loading area, too. It's like a bad film I didn't ask to see. It just flashes right up there in my mind when I'm not expecting it.
Since the explosion, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of the event?

Yeah, I have. I've been keeping away from the new building entirely. I just haven't gone over there at all. And... well, it's not just the site itself. Even some of my paperwork is getting to me. The mortgage folder, the safety reports—they're just sitting on my desk, completely unopened. It's strange, but the minute I even reach for them, my stomach just drops. So I just end up leaving them be.
Since the explosion, have you found yourself being more on edge, easily startled, or having trouble focusing on tasks that you normally wouldn't have issues with?

Yeah, I've definitely been more on edge lately. It's just... well, if a door shuts hard down the hall, or even if the printer just kicks on behind me, I jump. I jump like something went off again. And then, you know, it actually takes me a few minutes just to get my hands steady before I can go back to what I was doing.
Have these symptoms been causing you a lot of distress or making it hard for you to do things you need to do at work or at home?

Well, yeah, it is making things harder. I mean, I'm still technically working, still showing up, but... I'm putting off decisions about the facility. I just can't seem to make the call right now. And I'm leaning heavily on my team to handle things I'd normally just take care of myself. It really hit me during a board call recently—my reaction to something was just off, and it made me realize that this whole thing is actually starting to affect my judgment. It's messing with my ability to lead the way I need to.
How long have these symptoms been going on, and have they remained fairly consistent since the explosion?
It's been about six days now. Pretty much ever since the explosion and the fire happened during that walkthrough. And yeah, it's been pretty consistent since then.
Have you noticed that your symptoms only happen when you're reminded of the explosion and fire, or do they also come up even when you're not thinking about the event?

Well, it happens even when I'm not thinking about it at all. I could just be in the middle of a phone call, or sitting at my desk looking at some numbers, completely focused on work. And then, out of nowhere, the blast and that fire down by the loading area just jump right back into my head. It's... well, it's like a bad film I didn't ask to see just starts playing. So, yeah, it definitely comes up on its own, even when I'm trying to focus on other things.
Have you been having trouble falling or staying asleep since the explosion, or experiencing any nightmares related to it?
No, I haven't really had any trouble with that. I've been sleeping fine, honestly. And no nightmares about the explosion either. It's just during the day when it keeps popping into my head.
Have you noticed any improvement in these symptoms, or have they stayed just as intense as they were in the beginning?
They've stayed pretty much the same. I haven't really noticed them getting any better or worse, just... consistent, I guess. It's just as intense now as it was a few days ago.
Have you found yourself acting or feeling as though the explosion and fire are happening again when these memories come back to you?

No, I haven't had anything like that. I mean, the memory is strong, but I always know where I am. I don't feel like I'm actually back there in the middle of it again, or act like the fire is right in front of me. It's just... well, it's just a really vivid memory playing in my head. I know I'm still just sitting at my desk.
